title: Prioritize multi-language client bindings and resumable streaming ergonomics for enterprise onboarding
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Consolidate and prioritize incoming enterprise requests for SDK language bindings (Go, Rust, Kotlin, Java), enterprise-grade auth patterns (SSO/SAML, token rotation, delegated credentials), and streaming ergonomics (resumable streams, client-side backpressure, reconnect strategies). Deliver a prioritization rubric and an actionable roadmap that the engineering and design teams can execute against in the next two quarters.
background: We continue to see an elevated volume of enterprise intake asking for native client libraries in languages beyond Node/Python, plus higher-assurance auth patterns and better streaming ergonomics for long-running sessions (agent loops, file uploads, real-time assistants).
Current ad-hoc handling causes long SLAs for enterprise onboarding; some deals are stalled because of unclear priorities and engineering bandwidth.
Existing docs and playbooks are fragmented (see linked artifacts). We need a single prioritized path that balances revenue, security requirements, and engineering effort.
customer_signals: Three enterprise prospects (fintech, healthcare, e-comm) explicitly listed language bindings as gating
Support tickets requesting resumable streaming + token rotation for >30min sessions
Customer success feedback: developer experience issues when integrating streaming SDK wrappers (friction in reconnection and message ordering)
acceptance_criteria: Publish a prioritization rubric that scores requests on customer value, legal/security complexity, engineering effort, and strategic fit.
Deliver a ranked backlog with at least 6 concrete work items (eg. Go binding MVP, resumable-stream spec, delegated-credentials flow sample).
Define engineering owners and acceptance criteria for the top-3 items and link to ENG tickets.
Create a short design spec for streaming ergonomics with example API surface, reconnect semantics, and UX notes for error cases.
Stakeholder alignment recorded (sales, solutions, support, ENG, design) and decision sign-off captured in decision_log.
proposal_summary: Phase 1 (MVP, 6 weeks): Implement thin language bindings (Go + Rust) that wrap our existing HTTP/streaming API, plus a resumable-streams client-side reference that supports checkpointing and token refresh hooks.
Phase 2 (polish, 8-12 weeks): Native idiomatic SDKs with batching helpers, connection pooling, and built-in backpressure; formal SAML/SSO flow guides and examples for enterprise IdPs.
Phase 3 (scale): Add Kotlin + Java idiomatic clients, hardened token rotation and credential delegation patterns, and performance benchmarks for each binding.
prioritization_rubric: Score components: CustomerRevenuePotential (0-5), NumberOfCustomersAffected (0-5), SecurityComplexity (0-5, higher = more blockers), EngineeringEffort (0-5, lower preferred), StrategicGap (0-5).

Example: Go binding requested by two P0 prospects (CRM vendor + fintech) -> CustomerRevenuePotential=5, NumberOfCustomersAffected=4, SecurityComplexity=2, EngineeringEffort=3, StrategicGap=4 => Weighted ~4.0 => P0
tradeoffs_and_risks: Building idiomatic native SDKs upfront increases developer delight but costs 3-4x compared to thin wrappers. We recommend starting with thin wrappers to accelerate time-to-value.
Resumable streams require standardizing checkpoints and server-side tolerances; naive implementation can exacerbate ordering/duplication issues.
Token rotation interplay with long-lived connections increases attack surface; security review must be early and explicit.
Supporting many languages concurrently risks fragmenting QA and docs; prioritize a staggered roll-out and cross-language parity plan.
decision_log: 2025-03-11: Agreed to prioritize thin wrappers (Go + Rust) for MVP and invest in a streaming ergonomics spec. (Aisha, Liam, Mei Chen - Solutions)
2025-03-14: Security flagged delegated-credentials pattern as requiring KMS/HSM integration - moved to Phase 2 gating. (Ravi Patel - Security)
2025-03-17: Sales committed two demos contingent on Go binding & resumable stream robustness; moved those items to top of P0 backlog. (Niels Berg - Sales)
implementation_plan: Create ENG tickets: ENG-83412 (Go thin wrapper + integration tests), ENG-83413 (Rust thin wrapper), ENG-83414 (Resumable stream reference + checkpoint API), ENG-83415 (Auth rotation hooks + samples)
Design: DES-1245 to produce API surface recommendations and error-state UX flows for streaming reconnects.
Security: Kickoff security review in sprint 12 for token rotation and delegated credentials patterns.
Customer validation: Prepare demo scripts and run with two committed prospects in April for early feedback.
next_steps: Create the ENG tickets listed and link back to this PM ticket (owner: Liam) - due 2025-03-21.
Design to deliver a 2-page API spec + example code snippets for resumable streams by 2025-03-28.
Schedule weekly sync with Sales/CS to surface new incoming enterprise requests; capture into the rubric spreadsheet.
Prep a lightweight developer survey to capture friction points from partners integrating streaming APIs.
notes: Aim to keep initial bindings as a thin compatibility layer to minimize divergence from the core HTTP/streaming surface.
Consider open-sourcing thin wrappers after alpha to accelerate community contributions and broaden testing across language versions.
Measure success with: time-to-first-successful-integration (days), number of enterprise deals unblocked, and number of streaming reconnections without data loss in demo scenarios.
